# DeviceTypes

Added in [API level 30](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

# DeviceTypes

Kotlin| [Java](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/service/controls/DeviceTypes "View this page in Java") 

```
open class DeviceTypes
```

| [kotlin.Any](https://kotlinlang.org/api/latest/jvm/stdlib/kotlin/-any/index.html) ||
| ↳ | [android.service.controls.DeviceTypes](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/service/controls/DeviceTypes#) |

Device types for [Control](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/service/controls/Control). Each [Control](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/service/controls/Control) declares a type for the device they represent. This type will be used to determine icons and colors.

The type of the device may change on status updates of the [Control](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/service/controls/Control). For example, a device of [TYPE_OUTLET](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/service/controls/DeviceTypes#TYPE_OUTLET:kotlin.Int) could be determined by the [ControlsProviderService](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/service/controls/ControlsProviderService) to be a [TYPE_COFFEE_MAKER](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/service/controls/DeviceTypes#TYPE_COFFEE_MAKER:kotlin.Int) and change the type for that [Control](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/service/controls/Control), therefore possibly changing icon and color.

In case the device type is not know by the application but the basic function is, or there is no provided type, one of the generic types (those starting with`TYPE_GENERIC`) can be used. These will provide an identifiable icon based on the basic function of the device.
